item.text: {"text":"Research supports controlling negative hardness rather than always selecting the highest-scoring items. [UFNRec (SDM 2023)](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611977653.ch6) identifies likely false negatives and reverses their labels, stabilizing supervision with EMA and consistency regularization; its full method would require checking compatibility with the single-model constraint. [Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) selects negatives with appropriate hardness to mitigate false-positive and false-negative problems, although evaluated for collaborative filtering rather than specifically BERT4Rec. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates catalog softmax through selective maximum-inner-product computations, offering an alternative to weak random-negative supervision.\n\nNo verified result from this search establishes the exact combination of BERT4Rec, false-negative-aware sampled softmax, and jointly trained title/description embeddings initialized from scratch. [DenseRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18442) studies content integration but uses pretrained representations, so is not directly admissible here. A testable adaptation: retain terminal masking and appended-mask inference; jointly train a small text encoder inside the same BERT4Rec network; mix uniform candidates with moderately hard model/text-derived candidates; exclude known training positives and downweight uncertain semantic near-duplicates instead of automatically relabeling them. This is a proposed experiment, not an established improvement. Nonuniform sampling needs explicit consideration of proposal probabilities; deterministic top-k mining should not be described as unbiased sampled softmax. Compare against uniform sampled softmax using host macro validation HR@10, with one checkpoint per category."}
